name: Anesthesiology
tag: Call model, ASA units, supervision ratio, CRNA/AA model, cases, post-call recovery, group stability.
questions: What is the call schedule and post-call policy?
What is the CRNA/AA supervision ratio?
Is compensation salary, unit-based, or blended?

samples.name: Hospital Anesthesia Group
samples.pros: Stable hospital support and predictable benefits.
samples.cons: Clarify call, post-call recovery, staffing shortages, and extra shift pay.

samples.name: Private Anesthesia Partnership Track
samples.cons: Hospital contract risk, buy-in, call intensity, and tail must be understood.

samples.name: ASC-Focused Anesthesia Role
samples.cons: Lower upside and multisite travel possible.

Compensation: Is compensation salary, ASA unit-based, call-stipend-based, shift-based, or blended?
Are extra shifts, late rooms, weekends, holidays, OB call, cardiac call, or backup call paid separately?
Is compensation pooled equally or tied to individual productivity?
Are stipends from the hospital passed through to physicians?
Are there sign-on, retention, relocation, or loan repayment bonuses?
What happens to income if rooms close, staffing is short, or hospital volume drops?
Clinical model: What is the CRNA/AA supervision or medical direction ratio by site?
How much work is solo versus medical direction?
What cases are required: OB, cardiac, peds, trauma, neuro, regional, ASC, endoscopy?
How many sites are covered, and is travel between sites required?
What is the pre-op, PACU, acute pain, block, and airway support structure?
APP / CRNA / AA supervision: Is CRNA/AA supervision compensated separately or built into salary?
Is pay different for 1:2, 1:3, or 1:4 supervision?
Who handles breaks, handoffs, emergency coverage, and documentation?
Are medical direction billing requirements supported operationally?
Who owns liability for supervised anesthetics?
Quality bonus: Are metrics tied to on-time starts, cancellations, patient satisfaction, complications, block success, documentation, or throughput?
What is the maximum quality bonus and historical average payout?
Are quality metrics individual, group, hospital, or department-wide?
Lifestyle / call: How many calls per month, nights, weekends, and holidays?
How are vacations assigned and protected?
Can physicians reduce call later in career?
Contract risk: Is malpractice occurrence or claims-made, and who pays tail?
What happens if the hospital contract changes or is lost?
Is there a noncompete or nonsolicit?
Are stipend, sign-on, relocation, or loan payments clawed back?

Clinical Fit: Case mix, acuity, regional/cardiac/OB/peds expectations match training.
CRNA/AA supervision model is safe and operationally supported.
Compensation Upside: ASA units, call stipends, extra shifts, late rooms, and hospital stipends are transparent.
Lifestyle Fit: Call frequency, post-call recovery, nights, holidays, and vacation process are sustainable.
Risk Safety: Hospital contract risk, tail, noncompete, and clawbacks are acceptable.
Strategic Fit: Governance, partnership, leadership, and subspecialty development paths exist.
Collaborative Fit: Surgeons, OR leadership, CRNAs/AAs, PACU, and hospital administration collaborate well.
